meta.fun_fact: Irish Hills sits just outside the village of Carp, ON — home to the Diefenbunker, Canada's Cold War nuclear bunker. Built in 1959 to shelter 535 government officials, it was kept secret for decades and is now a national museum.

reviews.text: Greens were terrible — like putting on gravel. Not sure who is maintaining them but they need a serious upgrade.
Showed up for our tee time and they had double-booked the slot. Staff shrugged. Somehow still charged us a cancellation fee.
Course conditions were shocking for the price. Fairways were patchy, divots everywhere, and the cart path nearly destroyed my suspension.
Tee boxes are basically dirt patches at this point. Paid full price to hit off what felt like a construction site.
In the Spring, the mosquitos and blackflies can be thick. Spent more time swatting than swinging.
Some fairways need top dressing badly. Inconsistent conditions throughout — you'll have a great hole then a disaster.

stops.name: Carp Custom Creamery
stops.desc: Local institution. Real cream, huge scoops, unique flavours like Skoreo, raspberry cheesecake, and banoffee pie. People drive 40km just for this. Milkshakes too.

stops.name: Carp Bakery
stops.desc: Family-run bakery right in the village. Legendary cinnamon buns — light, fresh, and barely sweet. Sourdough that gets shipped back to BC. Show up early before they sell out.

stops.name: Skylark Café
stops.desc: Perfect 5.0 rating. Cosy, welcoming café right in Carp village. Handmade tables, great coffee, homemade sandwiches and gluten-free treats. The owner made every detail herself.

stops.name: Alice's Village Café
stops.desc: Beloved local spot with 1,371 reviews. The big cinnamon bun is not to be missed. Fresh soups, flatbreads, and salads. Closes at 3pm so time it right after the round.

stops.name: VANILLE Café & Bakery
stops.desc: New family-owned café on Stittsville Main. French pastries, almond croissants, macarons. The pistachio royal latte and honey almond latte are standouts.

stops.name: Bonnechere Bakery & Bistro
stops.desc: The all-rounder — bakery counter for the road, full bistro for the eat-in crowd. Bright open space, strong coffee, sandwiches that show up at lunch. Closes at 3 on Saturdays so don't dawdle.

stops.name: Stacked Pancake & Breakfast House
stops.desc: Exactly what you want after a 6am tee — fluffy pancakes, fast service, big portions. Reliable chain energy in a town that doesn't have many full-service breakfast spots open weekend mornings.

stops.name: Step'N Back Diner
stops.desc: Down-home diner with the locals. Memorabilia-on-the-walls energy, hearty plates, gluten-free toast on request, and friendly servers who know everyone. Cash-friendly and fast.

stops.name: Odi's Kingburger Drive-In
stops.desc: Renfrew institution. The Kingburger sauce is famous, curly fries are a 10, and locals defend it like a religion. Opens at 11 — line up the round so you walk in right at opening for a late-morning lunch.

scorecards.course: Timber Run Golf Club & Event Lodge

stops.name: Penny's Place
stops.desc: The post-round play. Big-portion homemade breakfast — Supreme Hash bowls, the Keto bowl, generous coffee top-ups. Hits exactly when you walk off at 11am. Closes at 3pm, so don't dawdle.

stops.name: The Fieldhouse Bakery
stops.desc: Cruffins, flaky chocolate croissants warmed on request, sandwiches sized like a meal. Patio out back, mochas worth the stop. Quieter alternative to Penny's if you just want pastry and coffee.

stops.name: Basic Kneads Bakery
stops.desc: European-quality bread baked that morning — chili-oil focaccia, sourdough rye, cobbler loaves. Grab one to bring home; they go fast. Order ahead if you want guaranteed pickup.

stops.name: The Rideau Candy Shoppe
stops.desc: Tiny downtown shop, outsized selection. Kawartha ice cream by the scoop plus a wall of candy older than most of us. The kind of stop that turns into a 20-minute browse.

meta.fun_fact: Château Cartier Golf Course opened in 1923 and sits on the banks of the Ottawa River, offering views of the Champlain Bridge rapids and Parliament Hill's Peace Tower. It's considered one of Canada's best downtown golf resort experiences.

reviews.text: Fairways lacking grass, tee boxes essentially no grass and hard to place your tee, greens not well kept, bumpy. Same high-end price though!
Half of the yardage markers on the tees are facing the wrong way, and some holes almost seem to overlap. Dangerous.
The condos have taken over! The first and 18th holes are terrible. Hole 18 is somewhere around 50-60 yards long.
I am always concerned before crossing the road along the river to play the 4th hole as car traffic is important and people drive like maniacs.
The folks at Cartier need to take a lesson in customer service and get their business straightened out with Chrono Golf. Avoid this golf course.
Ok but not in great shape. There are a lot of overlapping holes which I think is dangerous. A few interesting holes but too many dull ones.

stops.name: Boulangerie Aux Deux Frères
stops.desc: 4.9 stars from 474 reviews. Best croissants and chocolatines in Aylmer. Small place, fresh baked daily — get there before they sell out.

stops.name: Maison Oddo
stops.desc: One of the best patisseries in the Ottawa-Gatineau region. A French diplomat reportedly drives 25 minutes every day just for the croissants. Borderline unreasonable.

stops.name: les cafés Aroma Select
stops.desc: Best coffee in the NCR according to regulars. Freshly roasted and ground on-site. Staff match you to the perfect roast. Also carries tea, spices, and chocolate.

stops.name: Café Mulligan
stops.desc: Cosy locally owned café with heart and soul. Exceptional mochas, fresh food, gluten-free options. Closes at 3pm — head straight there after the round.

stops.name: Chocolats Favoris
stops.desc: Specialty chocolate-dipped ice cream. The dip is absurdly thick — get the cone filled with fondant at the bottom for the full experience. Order a small.

stops.name: Fidélice – Artisan gourmet
stops.desc: Stunning artisan cakes and pastries. The chocolate mousse cake Évasion is legendary. Gluten-free options available. Worth the slightly longer drive.

meta.fun_fact: Pine View opened in 1972 as a City of Ottawa municipal course before new ownership took over in 2014. It's one of Ottawa's only 36-hole facilities, pairing the Championship course with an Executive layout designed by famed Canadian architect Graham Cooke.

reviews.text: Course deteriorated in the last year. Greens and tee boxes are in horrible shape. Clubhouse stinks. Washrooms filthy.
Somehow the greens west of Ottawa are in much better shape. Dragonfly, Cobden, Mountain Creek — all better. Many of the greens here are like gravel roads interrupted by mud spots.
With all the great courses in the Ottawa area I cannot think of a good reason to play this course other than price and availability.

food.name: Oh My Choco
food.desc: Waffles, crepes, and hot chocolate made with real melted milk chocolate. Rocky road and Ferrero waffles are the move. Open from 4pm — perfectly timed for a post-round treat.

food.name: Breadwinners Sandwich & Bakery
food.desc: Gourmet sandwiches that rival Little Italy's best. The Porkfolio — prosciutto, capicolla, salami, fresh mozzarella, balsamic glaze — is the one. People drive across the city for it. Closed Mondays.

food.name: Geenie Bakery
food.desc: Lebanese meat and cheese pies so good people make special trips across town. Ask for lemon and spice on the meat pies. Cash and debit only — no credit cards.

food.name: Dao Cafe
food.desc: Trendy café with a cult following for their crème brûlée croissant. Cozy atmosphere, good coffee, open late every day — no need to rush off the back nine.

food.name: Milo's Pastry
food.desc: Custom cakes and artisan pastries made to order. The tiramisu has a devoted following and the strawberry shortcake is a crowd favourite. Closed Mondays.

stops.name: Equator Coffee Gloucester
stops.desc: Closest stop to the first tee, tucked inside the Chapters at Blair. Ottawa-roasted Equator coffee, friendly baristas who'll dial in your order, plus light baked goods.

stops.name: Mezzaluna Bakery & Pastry
stops.desc: Stunning croissants, pistachio rolls, and a Basque cheesecake regulars rave about — rich but light. Opens early, so it works before or after the round.

stops.name: Oh My Choco
stops.desc: Loaded waffles, crepes, and ice cream with real melted-chocolate hot chocolate. Cozy, generous, board games on the tables. Opens at noon on Saturdays.

stops.name: The Merry Dairy
stops.desc: An Ottawa institution — fresh frozen custard and rotating small-batch flavours, with plenty of vegan options. Worth the detour west on the way home.
